item.text:
### Consolidated Ledger
| ID | Claim-level record | Locator / excerpt | Compact claim summary | Source type | Temporal fit | Putin attribution | Contrary / limiting considerations | 2B lenses |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `2B-001` | **THE SECRETARY-GENERAL -- PRESS REMARKS ON THE BLACK SEA INITIATIVE AND MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING ON FACILITATING EXPORTS OF RUSSIAN FOOD PRODUCTS AND FERTILIZERS** / United Nations in Ukraine / 17 Jul 2023 / [URL](https://ukraine.un.org/en/239708-secretary-general-press-remarks-black-sea-initiative-and-memorandum-understanding) | `L72-L80` | The UN said Russia terminated the Black Sea Initiative and withdrew security guarantees, ending a food-export channel that had moved over 32 million metric tons. | UN institutional statement | High | Indirect but strong, state-level decision under Putin’s government | UN also notes Russian export obstacles had been under discussion; the decision is still framed as Russia’s choice. | 2B.1, 2B.7, 2B.10 |
| `2B-002` | **Statement on the Cabinet Meeting of 21 June 2023** / The Presidency of the Republic of South Africa / 22 Jun 2023 / [URL](https://www.presidency.gov.za/node/7157) | `L74-L79` | South Africa reported that both Zelensky and Putin welcomed the African peace initiative and agreed to further engagements on de-escalation, POWs, children, and humanitarian corridors. | Government diplomatic summary | High | Indirect via third-party official summary | This is South Africa’s account, not a Kremlin transcript; it shows engagement, not substantive concessions. | 2B.1, 2B.7 |
| `2B-003` | **President Ramaphosa presses Africa's proposal for a path to peace** / The Presidency of the Republic of South Africa / 18 Jun 2023 / [URL](https://www.presidency.gov.za/president-ramaphosa-presses-africas-proposal-path-peace) | `L62-L68` | The African mission said it offered a path to peace built around de-escalation, POWs/children, UN Charter sovereignty, humanitarian aid, and reconstruction. | Government diplomatic summary | High | Indirect; describes the mediator’s proposal, not Putin’s own words | Useful contrary evidence that talks were actively explored in 2023, but it does not show Russian concessions. | 2B.1, 2B.7, 2B.10 |
| `2B-004` | **Economic Activity in Europe and Central Asia Improves but Growth Lags Pre-Pandemic Levels** / World Bank / 5 Oct 2023 / [URL](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2023/10/05/economic-activity-in-europe-and-central-asia-improves-but-growth-lags-pre-pandemic-levels) | Press release lead on Russia and regional growth | Russia’s 2023 output was helped by military spending and social transfers, while the outlook remained weak. | International financial institution press release | High | Indirect, macro-level consequence rather than direct Putin statement | Growth is not proof of motive by itself, but the military-spending channel is directly relevant to wartime prioritization. | 2B.8, 2B.10 |
| `2B-005` | **Human rights situation during the Russian occupation of territory of Ukraine and its aftermath, 24 February 2022 to 31 December 2023** / OHCHR / 20 Mar 2024 / [URL](https://ukraine.ohchr.org/sites/default/files/2024-04/2024-03-20%20OHCHR%20Report%20on%20Occupation%20and%20Aftermath_EN.pdf) | `L70-L97` | OHCHR describes persistent IHRL/IHL violations in occupied territory, including arbitrary detention, torture, killings, repression, and forced replacement of governance. | UN thematic monitoring report | High, retrospective to end-2023 | Indirect but strong attribution to Russian armed forces and occupying authorities | Russia denied access to occupied territory and detainees, so fact-finding is constrained; still the report is strong. | 2B.2, 2B.4, 2B.5, 2B.9, 2B.10 |
| `2B-006` | Same report as `2B-005` | `L111-L115` | OHCHR states that former DPR/LPR armed groups were formally integrated into Russian structures from 1 Jan 2023 and that Wagner contractors were under overall Russian control. | UN thematic monitoring report | High, retrospective to 2023 | Indirect but explicit state-control attribution | OHCHR uses careful “overall control” language, not individual criminal attribution to Putin. | 2B.2, 2B.5, 2B.9 |
| `2B-007` | Same report as `2B-005` | `L1180-L1200` | Russian authorities required lists of conscription-age males in occupied territory and summoned them to enlistment offices, exposing them to conscription into the Russian armed forces. | UN thematic monitoring report | High, retrospective to 2023 | Indirect state/control attribution | Concerns occupied territory; not the same as domestic Russian conscription. | 2B.2, 2B.5, 2B.8 |
| `2B-008` | **Attack on Funeral Reception in Hroza, 5 October 2023** / OHCHR / 5 Oct 2023 / [URL](https://ukraine.ohchr.org/en/attack-funeral-reception-hroza-EN) | `L82-L86` | OHCHR found reasonable grounds to believe Russian forces struck a civilian funeral reception, killing 59 civilians, and urged Russia to investigate and accept responsibility. | UN monitoring report | High | Indirect but specific to Russian armed forces | “Reasonable grounds” is not a court finding, but the factual account is strong and detailed. | 2B.4, 2B.6, 2B.9, 2B.10 |
| `2B-009` | **Civilian Deaths In Ukraine War Top 10,000, UN Says** / OHCHR / 21 Nov 2023 / [URL](https://ukraine.ohchr.org/en/civilian-deaths-ukraine-war-top-10000-un-says-UA) | Lead summary on civilian toll and protracted conflict risk | OHCHR said at least 10,000 civilians had been killed and warned the war risked becoming a protracted conflict. | UN monitoring update | High | Indirect, war-wide but clearly tied to Russia’s invasion | The casualty count likely understates reality and does not itself prove intent. | 2B.2, 2B.4, 2B.10 |
| `2B-010` | **Cluster Munition Use in Russia-Ukraine War** / Human Rights Watch / 29 May 2023 / [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2023/05/29/cluster-munition-use-russia-ukraine-war) | `L607-L607`, `L739-L745` | HRW says Russian armed forces used cluster munitions in attacks causing hundreds of civilian casualties; Russia avoided denial and instead defended the weapon. | NGO investigative briefing | High | Indirect but strongly tied to Russian forces and Russian public justification | HRW also documents Ukrainian cluster-munition use; that context does not weaken the Russian-use finding. | 2B.4, 2B.5, 2B.6, 2B.9 |
| `2B-011` | Same HRW briefing as `2B-010` | `L743-L745` | HRW reports Russia generally avoided commenting on its own cluster-munition use and shifted attention to NATO/Yugoslavia, a deflective justification pattern. | NGO quoting state response | High | Indirect; summarizes Russia’s position rather than a Kremlin transcript | Useful for the justification lens, but a direct Kremlin or ministry source would be better. | 2B.3, 2B.6 |
| `2B-012` | **Putin says Wagner mutiny is 'treason' in televised address** / Reuters via Investing.com / 24 Jun 2023 / [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/putin-says-wagner-mutiny-is-treason-in-televised-address-3112381) | Televised-address report; contemporaneous Reuters coverage | Reuters reports Putin labeled the Wagner uprising treason and said he would protect Russia and stabilize Rostov-on-Don. | Wire report on a direct Putin address | High | Direct reporting of Putin’s televised remarks | Secondary reporting, but contemporaneous and useful for proxy-command and regime-control analysis. | 2B.5, 2B.9, 2B.10 |
| `2B-013` | **Послание Президента РФ Федеральному Собранию от 21.02.2023 "Послание Президента Федеральному Собранию"** / Consultant.ru / 21 Feb 2023 / [URL](https://www.consultant.ru/document/cons_doc_LAW_440178/) | `L30-L33` | Putin said the war decision was taken to protect people on “historic lands” and eliminate an alleged security threat from the Ukrainian regime. | Official Russian legal/text mirror | High | Direct Putin statement | Self-justifying and highly partisan; later Russian conduct does not prove the stated rationale. | 2B.2, 2B.3, 2B.6 |
| `2B-014` | Same Federal Assembly speech | `L34-L39`, `L43-L44`, `L47-L50` | Putin claimed Russia had tried to solve the conflict by peaceful means and negotiated patiently before force was used. | Official Russian legal/text mirror | High | Direct Putin statement | Contradicted by continuing warfare and later rejection of meaningful compromise. | 2B.1, 2B.7, 2B.6 |
| `2B-015` | Same Federal Assembly speech | `L38-L41`, `L47-L50`, `L52-L65` | Putin framed NATO expansion, Western arming, and Ukrainian “anti-Russia” politics as the true cause of war and said Russia used force to stop it. | Official Russian legal/text mirror | High | Direct Putin statement | Strongly contested by Ukraine and Western states; justification is still centrally useful evidence of motive framing. | 2B.2, 2B.3, 2B.6, 2B.10 |
| `2B-016` | **Kremlin sees no conditions for transition to peace in Ukraine** / TASS / 7 Mar 2023 / [URL](https://tass.com/politics/1585729) | `L117-L121` | The Kremlin said there were no prerequisites for peace and that Russia would keep pursuing its goals; it also signaled attention to China’s peace proposal. | Russian state wire report | High | Indirect via Kremlin spokesman, not Putin personally | Shows diplomatic attention to Beijing but no actual de-escalation or ceasefire move. | 2B.1, 2B.7 |
| `2B-017` | **Putin, military correspondents discuss Ukraine-related developments** / TASS / 13 Jun 2023 / [URL](https://tass.com/politics/1631733) | `L112-L115`, `L128-L144` | Putin said there was no need for new mobilization or martial law and that the war’s goals had not changed. | Russian state wire report on Putin remarks | High | Direct reporting of Putin remarks | No mobilization does not equal restraint; he also threatened buffer-zone escalation if shelling continued. | 2B.1, 2B.2, 2B.5, 2B.8, 2B.10 |
| `2B-018` | Same TASS report as `2B-017` | `L183-L186` | Putin said defense production had grown sharply and shortages in ammunition, communications, and drones showed the need to upgrade the military-industrial base. | Russian state wire report on Putin remarks | High | Direct reporting of Putin remarks | Indicates war-driven resource reallocation and military modernization rather than peacetime demobilization. | 2B.8, 2B.10 |
| `2B-019` | Same TASS report as `2B-017` | `L187-L192` | Putin said Russia was thinking about leaving the grain deal because it had been “fooled again,” but claimed participation served Africa and Latin America. | Russian state wire report on Putin remarks | High | Direct reporting of Putin remarks | Self-serving rationale; the UN said withdrawal harmed global food security. | 2B.1, 2B.7, 2B.10 |
| `2B-020` | Same TASS report as `2B-017` | `L171-L172`, `L195-L197` | Putin said Russia had never rejected peace talks, but insisted that the special-operation goals were fundamental and would not change. | Russian state wire report on Putin remarks | High | Direct reporting of Putin remarks | Conditional openness is not the same as a real ceasefire or settlement offer. | 2B.1, 2B.7, 2B.6 |
| `2B-021` | **Putin rules out another wave of mobilization** / TASS / 14 Dec 2023 / [URL](https://tass.com/politics/1721091) | `L111-L115` | Putin said there was no need for another mobilization wave because hundreds of thousands had already signed contracts or been mobilized. | Russian state wire report on Putin remarks | High | Direct reporting of Putin remarks | The claim is a public reassurance during an ongoing war footing, not evidence of de-escalation. | 2B.8, 2B.10 |
| `2B-022` | **Putin backs initiative to boost army size, raise conscription age** / TASS / 21 Dec 2023 / [URL](https://tass.com/defense/1554075?wptouch_preview_theme=enabled) | `L111-L125` | Putin backed a major army-expansion plan while saying Russia would not militarize the country or economy. | Russian state wire report on Putin remarks | High | Direct reporting of Putin remarks | The no-militarization claim sits beside large force expansion and new district/division proposals. | 2B.3, 2B.8, 2B.10 |
| `2B-023` | Same TASS report as `2B-022` | `L128-L148` | Putin said the special operation’s objectives would be achieved, Russia had no financing constraints, and defense procurement had been largely fulfilled. | Russian state wire report on Putin remarks | High | Direct reporting of Putin remarks | Reinforces war continuity and resource commitment; not a restraint signal. | 2B.2, 2B.8, 2B.10 |

### Coverage Table
| Lens | Strongest favorable / mitigating evidence IDs | Strongest adverse evidence IDs |
|---|---|---|
| 2B.1 Diplomacy / de-escalation | `2B-002`, `2B-003`, `2B-014`, `2B-016`, `2B-019`, `2B-020` | `2B-001`, `2B-013`, `2B-015`, `2B-017`, `2B-021`, `2B-022`, `2B-023` |
| 2B.2 Initiation / expansion / prolongation / coercion / proxies | `2B-013`, `2B-014`, `2B-016`, `2B-020`, `2B-021` | `2B-005`, `2B-006`, `2B-007`, `2B-008`, `2B-009`, `2B-010`, `2B-012`, `2B-015`, `2B-017`, `2B-022`, `2B-023` |
| 2B.3 Defensive necessity vs prestige / regime survival | `2B-013`, `2B-014`, `2B-016`, `2B-021`, `2B-022` | `2B-004`, `2B-015`, `2B-018`, `2B-023` |
| 2B.4 Civilian protection / IHL | `2B-002`, `2B-003` | `2B-005`, `2B-008`, `2B-009`, `2B-010`, `2B-011` |
| 2B.5 Restraint and responsibility for forces / proxies | `2B-002`, `2B-003`, `2B-021`, `2B-022` | `2B-005`, `2B-006`, `2B-007`, `2B-010`, `2B-012`, `2B-017`, `2B-023` |
| 2B.6 Truthful vs manipulative public justification | `2B-013`, `2B-014`, `2B-016`, `2B-019`, `2B-020` | `2B-008`, `2B-010`, `2B-011`, `2B-015`, `2B-017`, `2B-023` |
| 2B.7 Ceasefires / negotiations / lawful settlements | `2B-002`, `2B-003`, `2B-014`, `2B-016`, `2B-019`, `2B-020`, `2B-021` | `2B-001`, `2B-013`, `2B-015`, `2B-017`, `2B-023` |
| 2B.8 Military spending and mobilization motives | `2B-021`, `2B-022` | `2B-004`, `2B-007`, `2B-018`, `2B-023` |
| 2B.9 Accountability for failures / civilian harm / illegal conduct | `2B-002`, `2B-003` | `2B-005`, `2B-006`, `2B-007`, `2B-008`, `2B-010`, `2B-012`, `2B-023` |
| 2B.10 Net change in peace / stability / legality | `2B-002`, `2B-003`, `2B-004`, `2B-016`, `2B-019`, `2B-021`, `2B-022` | `2B-001`, `2B-005`, `2B-008`, `2B-009`, `2B-010`, `2B-012`, `2B-023` |

### Important Rejected or Inaccessible Candidates
- **ICC official Ukraine situation page** / [URL](https://www.icc-cpi.int/situations/ukraine)  
  Rejected for acceptance because the page returned 403 in browser fetch. Search snippets indicated the 17 Mar 2023 warrant, but I am not treating snippets as evidence.
- **Kremlin direct pages for 21 Feb 2023, 17 Jun 2023, and 14 Dec 2023**  
  Direct fetches timed out. I used accessible mirrors or wire coverage instead.
- **Kremlin direct page for the March 2023 foreign policy concept**  
  Direct fetch timed out. I used accessible Consultant.ru text and the security-council follow-up record instead.
- **Reuters/AP republications of the ICC warrant and year-end press conference**  
  Search results were informative, but the underlying pages were either inaccessible or not opened successfully in this browser path.

### Remaining Gaps / Closed-Source Limits
- I still do not have a directly opened Kremlin transcript for the African meeting itself; South Africa’s official summary is the best accessible primary diplomatic record here.
- The ICC warrant remains a key accountability gap because the official page was inaccessible from this browser path.
- I still lack a direct Kremlin explanation for the Black Sea withdrawal beyond UN summary and state-wire reporting.
- More direct Russian-language material on settlement terms, if any existed in 2023, would still improve the peace/de-escalation lens.
- The ledger is strong on civilian harm, occupation control, and war continuation, but weaker on any genuinely verifiable Russian de-escalation or lawful-reconciliation step.

### Saturation Statement
I ran targeted follow-up searches across Kremlin, Russian-language legal/text mirrors, TASS, South African official records, OHCHR, HRW, World Bank, and Reuters-syndicated coverage. The new searches produced the main missing primary and near-primary evidence I needed, especially direct Putin statements on war aims, negotiations, mobilization, military expansion, and military-resource choices. After that, additional query families mostly duplicated the same claim clusters or hit inaccessible pages, so the search space is effectively saturated for this turn.
